examples: We watched from afar.
She saw the lights from afar.
He waved from afar.

more.def: At or from a long way off.
examples: We watched the ship sail from afar.
The mountain could be seen from afar.
She admired the castle from afar.
The party was a grand affair.
That is my own affair.
It was a quiet affair.

more.def: An event, or a matter that someone is dealing with.
examples: The wedding was a grand affair.
What I do with my money is my own affair.
The school fair was a happy affair.

easy.def: To change something or have an effect on it.
examples: The rain will affect our picnic.
Sleep affects how you feel.
The cold affected the plants.

more.def: To cause a change in someone or something.
examples: The storm affected the whole town.
Too little sleep can affect how well you do at school.
Pollution can affect the fish in a river.
She showed affection for her pet.
The dog gave affection.
He hugged her with affection.

more.def: A warm, caring feeling that you have for someone.
examples: She showed affection by giving her sister a hug.
The puppy greeted us with affection.
Grandpa has great affection for his old dog.

easy.def: Showing love in a warm way.
examples: The dog is affectionate.
An affectionate hug.
She gave an affectionate pat.

more.def: Showing warm love and care for others, by hugging or being gentle.
examples: Our cat is very affectionate and loves to curl up in your lap.
She gave her grandmother an affectionate hug.
The affectionate puppy licked my hand.
She gave an affirmative nod.
His answer was affirmative.
We got an affirmative reply.

more.def: Meaning yes; agreeing with what was asked.
examples: The teacher gave an affirmative nod when I asked to go.
We got an affirmative reply from the coach about practice.
A nod of the head can be an affirmative answer.

easy.def: To have enough money for something.
examples: We can afford a new bike.
I cannot afford that toy.
They can afford a car.

more.def: To have enough money to pay for something.
examples: We saved money so we could afford a new bike.
The family could not afford a big house.
Can you afford a ticket to the show?
The shoes are affordable.
An affordable toy.
The price is affordable.

more.def: Not too expensive, so that most people can buy it.
examples: The shoes were affordable, so we bought two pairs.
The store sells affordable toys.
The family found an affordable house.
The boat stayed afloat.
Keep the raft afloat.
The toy is afloat.

more.def: Floating on water, or still able to keep going.
examples: The little boat stayed afloat in the waves.
We kept the raft afloat by patching the leak.
The small shop barely stayed afloat during the slow winter.
I am afraid of the dark.
The kitten is afraid of the vacuum.
Do not be afraid. I am here.

more.def: Feeling fear or worry that something bad might happen.
examples: The puppy was afraid of the loud thunder.
He was afraid to jump off the high diving board.
Many people are afraid of spiders, even small ones.
We play after school.
Rest after lunch.
She came after me.

more.def: At a later time than something, or following something.
examples: After the rain stopped, a rainbow appeared over the hills.
We will go to the park after dinner.
The ducklings walked one after another behind their mother.

easy.def: The time between lunch and dinner.
examples: We play in the afternoon.
The afternoon is sunny.
School ends in the afternoon.

more.def: The part of the day between noon and evening.
examples: We went swimming on a sunny afternoon.
The bus comes at three in the afternoon.
She naps every afternoon.

easy.def: A lotion for the face after shaving.
examples: Dad uses aftershave.
The aftershave smells good.
Grandpa wears aftershave.

more.def: A lotion with a strong smell that men put on their faces after shaving.
examples: Dad splashed aftershave on his cheeks.
The aftershave smelled like pine trees.
Grandpa kept a bottle of aftershave on the shelf.
We ate, and afterwards we played.
Afterwards, we went home.
I will call you afterwards.

more.def: At a later time, after something else has happened.
examples: We ate lunch and played outside afterwards.
The movie was fun, and afterwards we got ice cream.
Do your chores first and rest afterwards.
